title: per-invocation shared reads: one decisions parse, one cells scan, one transcript-root scan per status invocation
action: Thread a PER-INVOCATION shared-read structure, supplied by the caller, through the readers that repeat work — the same 'caller-supplied, never re-derived inside bee-core' convention rust-port-16 and rust-port-20 established for control_root and resolved_session_id. build_status loads each store ONCE and passes it down; build_recovery_block (recovery.rs:577) reuses what detect_crash_candidates already scanned at recovery.rs:457 instead of re-scanning at :586 — and the hoist must sit ABOVE the early return at recovery.rs:453-455, which returns before :457 when there are no session records; returning roots alongside candidates naively yields an empty roots block on exactly those fixtures; ceiling_scarcity_warning (cells.rs:442) consumes a tier_mix result rather than recomputing it. CALL SITES, from validation's own enumeration — note status.rs:539 (`list_cells (counts)`), which the earlier draft omitted: cells at status.rs:539, :640 (cells.rs:218 ready_cells), :708 (cells.rs:415 tier_mix), :712 (cells.rs:442), :742 (cells.rs:347), plus the conditional cells.rs:332 and recovery.rs:522; decisions at status.rs:790 (decisions.rs:56 and :120) plus the crash-candidate-gated recovery.rs:520; transcript roots at recovery.rs:586 plus the gated recovery.rs:457. THE ARCHIVE TRAP — READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING ready_cells (validation B3, the blocker most likely to ship silently): dep resolution goes through read_cell (cells.rs:208-213), whose contract at cells.rs:152-157 is that a dep missing from the active directory falls back to a search of .bee/cells/archive/*/<id>.json — note the FEATURE SUBDIRECTORY: cells.rs:171-178 reads the archive root, skips non-directories, and joins <id>.json inside each one (this repo currently has .bee/cells/archive/cells-archive/). A fixture written at .bee/cells/archive/<id>.json with no subdirectory is invisible to read_cell, so the required test would go red against unchanged code and the natural 'fix' would be to loosen it. With the correct path, dep resolution transparently sees archived capped deps. list_cells (cells.rs:99-126) skips archive/ at :108-116. Feeding ready_cells a pre-loaded ACTIVE-ONLY inventory therefore makes archived capped deps read as uncapped, and ready cells silently vanish from the recommendation line — with byte-parity still green, because the parity fixture has no archived deps. There is zero existing coverage for this. Either preserve the archive fallback explicitly in the shared-read shape, or leave dep resolution reading through read_cell untouched; whichever you choose, a test with an archived capped dep must fail if the fallback is lost. ALSO NAME AND SETTLE (validation W4): recovery.rs:332-343's last_durable_settlement re-reads decisions, capture and cells when its injected argument is None — it is public API and is the exact shape you are generalizing, so fold it into the same convention rather than leaving two competing SharedInputs shapes. WITHIN-INVOCATION CONSISTENCY IS A REAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (validation W5, wording corrected by advisor note 3): today the stores are read at roughly eight distinct instants, so a concurrent write mid-invocation can yield an internally inconsistent payload; after the dedup each store is read at ONE instant per invocation. Record it in exactly those terms — 'each store is read at one instant per invocation; cross-store consistency remains unguaranteed, exactly as today' — and NOT as 'snapshot semantics', which would overclaim: decisions, cells and transcripts are still loaded at distinct moments and a journal read racing an in-flight append is still possible. The frozen mjs oracle still re-reads, so under concurrent mutation the two runtimes differ; that is acceptable because nothing can legitimately depend on a torn read, and D3 contracts the stores' formats and semantics, not the reference implementation's incidental read count. Add NO concurrent-mutation differential test against the oracle — it would assert nondeterministic behaviour nobody contracted for and be flaky by construction. Note in the decision that status takes no D9 locks, so the lock and lease conformance surface is untouched. HOOK-PATH READS ARE PART OF THIS CELL'S PROOF (advisor note 1, the sixth blocker): the two hook entry points you are changing run per lifecycle event, and today chain-nudge's scribing_debt early-returns without any cells scan when no feature resolves. An eager shared-read shape would make that scan unconditional on every hook event with every verify leg still green. Re-assert rust-port-22's hook baselines after the change: chain-nudge with no active feature must still show zero cells scans, and conditional reads on the hook path must stay conditional. This is where your red-to-green transition lives on the consumer side. PRECEDENT: reviews.rs:44's GitMemo is an explicitly per-pass memo and recovery.rs:321-325's SharedInputs is the same idea scoped to one loop — extend that shape upward. REJECTED by the plan: a process-global or lazily-initialized static cache, and an on-disk cache like the review one (these stores change on every write, so the staleness guard that makes the review cache safe does not exist here). Byte-parity under single-threaded conditions is untouched: no field order, null-vs-absent, or degraded-block change. PLAN FILE IS STALE (cold-pickup C1): docs/history/rust-port/plan-slice3.md is frozen and still carries the superseded baseline numbers at :33/:52 and the ruled-out seam shape at :65; read it for approach, but rust-port-22's table and this cell supersede it on those points. GitMemo is at reviews.rs:302 (the :44 reference is module prose, not the type). CARRIED FORWARD FROM RUST-PORT-22'S ROUND-2 JUDGE — three facts about the instrument you are about to rely on. (1) THE COUNTERS SEE READERS, NOT THE FILESYSTEM. Every counter sits inside a specific function: the journal counter inside fsutil::read_jsonl (path-keyed), the cells counter inside cells::list_cells, the per-dep counter inside cells::read_cell, the transcript counters inside recovery::scan_transcript_roots. A hoisted loader that CALLS those functions is fully counted; a hoisted loader that REIMPLEMENTS one — a raw fs::read_dir of .bee/cells, a direct read_to_string of a cell file or of the journal, an inlined metadata loop — is invisible, and the judge measured this (a raw read_dir leaves the counter at 0 where list_cells gives 1). A silent-green 1/1/1 therefore remains reachable for the cells store: an uncounted hoisted scan plus the one surviving recovery scan reads as exactly 1. Load through the existing readers, never around them; if you must add a new load function, it goes through them or carries its own increment. (2) THE REGRESSION TEST'S CELLS HALF IS WEAKER THAN ITS DECISIONS HALF: it injects list_cells (the counted reader) rather than a raw read_dir, so it only catches a counter moved ABOVE list_cells. Do not treat it as covering the reimplementation hazard in (1). (3) THE ARCHIVE TRAP IS INVISIBLE TO THE INSTRUMENT: cell_dep_reads bundles read_cell's archive fallback, so losing that fallback moves no counter at all. Your archived-capped-dep test is the ONLY thing standing between this cell and that regression — it is not backed up by the read counts.

truths: the read-accounting instrument from rust-port-22 reports one read per store per build_status invocation on each fixture in its baseline table, using the same test and the same counter units that produced the baseline

an archived-capped-dep test proves ready_cells still resolves deps through the archive fallback, with the fixture written at .bee/cells/archive/<feature>/<id>.json (the feature subdirectory read_cell actually searches) — the test must fail if dep resolution is fed an active-only inventory
all six bee-parity status legs stay zero-diff with their per-leg mutation controls detected, and bee-parity --self-check stays green
every status-reader oracle target and both hook conformance targets stay green after the signature change — heavyhooks_conformance actually re-run, not merely recompiled
two invocations do not share a cache: a test proves a second invocation re-reads, so a write between invocations is observed
empty, absent and malformed stores read once and degrade exactly as they do today, proven against the mjs oracle

the within-invocation consistency change is LOGGED AS A DECISION through the decisions CLI (not only recorded in the trace), worded as 'one read instant per store, cross-store consistency still unguaranteed' — never as snapshot semantics — with the note that status takes no D9 locks

the hook entry points keep their read profile: chain-nudge with no active feature still shows zero cells scans after the change, and every read that was conditional on the hook path stays conditional — asserted with rust-port-22's hook baselines, not inferred from correctness tests

artifacts.substantive: caller-supplied shared reads threaded through decisions, cells and recovery readers, with dep resolution's archive fallback preserved
single load point per store per invocation, including the status.rs:539 counts read
chain-nudge and state-sync call sites moved to the new signatures

key_links: rust-port-22's instrument and its per-fixture baseline table are the proof surface
read_cell's archive fallback (cells.rs:152-157) is the trap this cell must not spring
GitMemo and SharedInputs are the per-invocation precedent; the on-disk review cache is deliberately not the model
rust-port-24 measures whether the budget can tighten
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
No process-global, static or on-disk cache — per invocation only
Never feed dep resolution an active-only inventory without preserving the archive fallback
No observable output change under single-threaded conditions (D3)
Tests never touch the live .bee/ store
No edits to crates/Cargo.toml members list

verify: cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p queen-bee && cargo test --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-core && cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --status-check && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --self-check

trace.outcome: Per-invocation shared reads: build_status now reads each store ONCE (decisions 4->1, cells 6->1, transcript roots 2->1). New bee_core::shared_reads::SharedReads is a caller-supplied, LAZY per-invocation memo (OnceCell, !Sync) that loads through the existing counted readers; recovery's competing SharedInputs is folded into it. Dep resolution deliberately still goes through read_cell, archive fallback intact. Hook read profiles re-asserted unchanged. status warm p95 52.6ms -> 26.96ms.
